- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially > -0.5) — reduce forecast by 5–10% in such regimes.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior day) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag in early days of a downward trend — adjust downward by 1–3% for the first 3–5 days of negative sentiment.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, forecast often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — use 3–5 day moving average sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a downtrend, forecast should not immediately rebound — wait 2–3 days before adjusting up.
